answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must register identities by locking funds across a dual-tier staking curve. Every identity tier follows superlinear cost scaling where burning cryptographic stake scales quadratically with network footprint. The protocol routes verification through localized clusters: a low-latency willow network handles sensor inputs, the mesa consensus layer enforces proof-of-burn slashing, and the lotus settlement mechanism levies exponential fees on replicated nodes. Attacker costs scale as O(N^2), rendering mass identity forgery economically unviable.
